Suppose $\dsn{X} \siid \ndist{\mean, \varpar}$,
and let $\dsn{x}$ be the observed values.
The parameter vector is $\vparam = (\mean, \varpar)$.
We treat $\varpar$, rather than $\sdpar$, as the second parameter,
and differentiate with respect to $\varpar$ directly.

By @thm-lik-iid, the likelihood is:

$$
\Lik(\mean, \varpar) = \prodin (2\pi\varpar)^{-1/2}
\expf{-\frac{(x_i - \mean)^2}{2\varpar}}
$$

and by @thm-loglik-iid, the log-likelihood is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\llik(\mean, \varpar)
&= \sumin \logf{(2\pi\varpar)^{-1/2}
\expf{-\frac{(x_i - \mean)^2}{2\varpar}}}
&& \text{(log of each Gaussian density)}\\
&= \sumin \paren{\logf{(2\pi\varpar)^{-1/2}}
 + \logf{\expf{-\frac{(x_i - \mean)^2}{2\varpar}}}}
&& \text{(log of a product)}\\
&= \sumin \paren{-\frac{1}{2}\logf{2\pi\varpar}
 + \logf{\expf{-\frac{(x_i - \mean)^2}{2\varpar}}}}
&& \text{(log of a power)}\\
&= \sumin \paren{-\frac{1}{2}\logf{2\pi\varpar} - \frac{(x_i - \mean)^2}{2\varpar}}
&& \text{($\logt$ undoes $\expt$)}\\
&= \sumin \paren{-\frac{1}{2}\logf{2\pi\varpar}}
 - \sumin \frac{(x_i - \mean)^2}{2\varpar}
&& \text{(split the sum)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\varpar}
 - \sumin \frac{(x_i - \mean)^2}{2\varpar}
&& \text{(sum of $n$ identical terms)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\varpar}
 - \frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{(factor the constant $\tfrac{1}{2\varpar}$ out of the sum)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\paren{\logf{2\pi} + \logf{\varpar}}
 - \frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{(log of a product)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi} - \frac{n}{2}\logf{\varpar}
 - \frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{(distribute $-\tfrac{n}{2}$)}
\end{aligned}
$$
